summary.text: The saved process declaration proposes a weather.forecast-updated mapping to Dashboard.consumeMessage; subscription settings and runtime delivery remain unverified. For that topic, validateEvent requires a string id, version 1, an allowed place id (oslo, helsinki, lisbon), string name, finite coordinates, type forecast.updated, valid updatedAt/fetchedAt timestamps, fixture or live mode, and 1–6 periods. Each period needs a valid time, finite temperature, null or finite nonnegative precipitation, and a string symbol. Parse or validation failures, including UNKNOWN_TOPIC, are caught, recorded as INVALID_EVENT, and followed by offset plus one; reject-write or offset-commit errors propagate. On valid input, applyEvent inserts the id into inbox in a transaction. A duplicate commits and returns DUPLICATE without changing the card. A new forecast can insert its card directly from event.place, without a prior place-requested event; an existing card updates only when its stored timestamp is null or older, while equal or older timestamps leave it unchanged and return OLDER_OR_EQUAL. Connected-client transaction errors attempt rollback and release in finally; connection errors occur before the try, and either failure prevents the offset commit. The DB transaction commits before the offset, so a later offset failure can replay the message; inbox suppresses a second card update, not duplicate delivery. Runtime remains unverified.

summary.text: The Dashboard source handler parses each message and validates the event against its topic. For invalid events, it attempts to insert a rejected_messages row with reason INVALID_EVENT (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), commits the next partition offset, and returns. For a valid event, it calls applyEvent before committing the next offset. The saved cross-service view associates this handler with weather.forecast-updated through an agent-proposed interaction; source subscription configuration and runtime delivery remain unverified. The effects inside applyEvent and Kafka behavior beyond these explicit handler calls are not established by this slice.

fragment.text: The saved process declaration proposes a weather.forecast-updated mapping to Dashboard.consumeMessage; subscription settings and runtime delivery remain unverified. For that topic, validateEvent requires a string id, version 1, an allowed place id (oslo, helsinki, lisbon), string name, finite coordinates, type forecast.updated, valid updatedAt/fetchedAt timestamps, fixture or live mode, and 1–6 periods. Each period needs a valid time, finite temperature, null or finite nonnegative precipitation, and a string symbol. Parse or validation failures, including UNKNOWN_TOPIC, are caught, recorded as INVALID_EVENT, and followed by offset plus one; reject-write or offset-commit errors propagate. On valid input, applyEvent inserts the id into inbox in a transaction. A duplicate commits and returns DUPLICATE without changing the card. A new forecast can insert its card directly from event.place, without a prior place-requested event; an existing card updates only when its stored timestamp is null or older, while equal or older timestamps leave it unchanged and return OLDER_OR_EQUAL. Connected-client transaction errors attempt rollback and release in finally; connection errors occur before the try, and either failure prevents the offset commit. The DB transaction commits before the offset, so a later offset failure can replay the message; inbox suppresses a second card update, not duplicate delivery. Runtime remains unverified.

fragment.text: The common envelope requires an object, string id, version 1, a place with id oslo, helsinki, or lisbon, string name, and finite latitude and longitude. The forecast branch requires updatedAt and fetchedAt accepted by isTimestamp, mode fixture or live, and a periods array of length 1 through 6. fragment.text: pool.connect runs before applyEvent's try. If it fails, there is no transaction rollback or client release. Once connected, errors inside the try attempt ROLLBACK, rethrow, and release the client in finally; either error prevents consumeMessage from reaching its valid-path offset commit. The DB transaction commits before the offset commit, so an offset failure can replay the message; the inbox duplicate check prevents a second card update, but does not establish exactly-once delivery.
